summary: A local feature on the heated debate over how to feed young athletes, covering carbohydrates, protein, sugar, hydration, organic food and supplements. For each topic, experts, coaches and parents give opposing views, mostly voiced at events from September to October 2023. The article concludes that the science is unsettled and the advice conflicting, leaving parents and coaches to sort through it.
one_line: Local article surveys conflicting expert and coach opinions on carbs, protein, sugar, hydration, organic food and supplements for young athletes.
key_facts: Dr. Nancy Clarkson, a sports nutritionist, says "complex carbohydrates are essential for sustained energy release, particularly in endurance sports."
Dr. Eric Vogel spoke at a nutritional seminar on September 5th, 2023, arguing that over-reliance on carbs can cause energy crashes and hinder performance, and advocating a low-carb, high-fat diet.
Samantha Peterson, a high school track coach, says her athletes need a lot of protein to build muscle and recover post-workout.
On September 22nd, nutritionist and author James Reed told a school PTA meeting that "Excess protein can strain young kidneys and leech calcium from growing bones."
Aaron Thompson, a youth basketball coach, defended giving sugary snacks during timeouts in an October 1st interview, saying "Nothing beats sugar when it comes to a rapid boost on the court."
Pediatrician Dr. Lisa Harper warned at a September 12th health symposium that regular sugary treats can cause erratic energy, mood swings and raise future diabetes risk.
Kevin Jones, an advocate for sports drinks, said at a September 28th soccer practice that "Water isn't enough" and that electrolytes help prevent cramps.
Pediatrician Dr. Margaret Liu argues sports drinks are packed with sugars and artificial additives, and that water should be "the gold standard for hydration."
A local football game on September 15th featured an "Organic Snack Stand"; local mom Jessica Trent said a chemical-free diet is vital for her child's performance and long-term health.
Critic and author Michael Dean said in an October 6th podcast that "The organic label often serves as little more than a marketing ploy."
A health fair on September 18th showcased many supplement brands touting benefits for performance, endurance and recovery.
Health expert David Langford says supplements can never replace a balanced diet and that the industry is under-regulated.
The article describes a vigorous debate among nutrition experts, coaches and parents that erupted as of late September 2023.
